decisions.statement: One seed gives one run of draws.
A draw is a whole number from nought up to but not including the bound asked for.
The run is arithmetic on the seed rather than the machine's own entropy.
A bound that is no positive whole number is refused rather than answered.
Two seeds that differ give runs that differ.
A draw asking for more items than there are gives every item there is.
The source of randomness is handed in rather than reached for.
An index the randomness returns from outside its bound is refused.

definition: items drawn without replacement from a source of draws a seed makes repeatable
